I am 65 years old and have farmed in Quzhou County for more than 40 years. I have five mu of good flat land, and I know every inch of it. At my age, I do not have the energy or the desire to experiment with new crops. Every year I plant winter wheat and summer maize — that is what our land and climate are suited for, that is what the grain buyers want, and that is what the government subsidizes. I already sowed my wheat last October after rotary tilling the fields. I used an improved variety like Jimai 22 because it yields better and resists lodging. Now, as the season starts, I am preparing to irrigate and topdress the wheat. After the wheat comes off in early June, I will immediately sow hybrid maize — Denghai 605 is what my neighbors and I have been using for years — and I will not bother tilling because there is barely ten days between wheat harvest and maize sowing; no-tillage works fine. I will irrigate the wheat four times and the maize twice. I apply compound fertilizer as a base and urea for topdressing; I have learned over the decades that this gives steady yields without wasting money. I spray when I see pests or when my neighbors start spraying — about four times per crop, mixing herbicide, insecticide, and fungicide as needed. I expect my wheat to yield around 550 kg per mu and my maize around 650 kg per mu. That is enough to feed my family, sell the surplus, and cover my costs.
